## Part A: Single Pathway Analysis

```{r}
head(data)
str(data)
dim(data)
names(data)
summary(data)

# Check missing values for each variable
colSums(is.na(data))

# Check duplicate participant IDs
sum(duplicated(data$ID))
```

```{r}
# Check whether values fall within the ranges
# specified in the assignment
summary(data$StatsCourses)
summary(data$GradeStats)
summary(data$Judgment)
summary(data$Comprehension)

# Check categorical variables
table(data$Sexe, useNA = "ifany")
table(data$GoalStudy, useNA = "ifany")
```

### 2. Descriptive Statistics
```{r}
data %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_stats_courses = mean(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_stats_courses = sd(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_judgment = mean(Judgment, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_judgment = sd(Judgment, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_comprehension = mean(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_comprehension = sd(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Distribution of the outcome variable
ggplot(data, aes(x = Judgment)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Judgement Scores",
    x = "Number of correct judgements",
    y = "Number of participants"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Association between statistics credits and judgement
ggplot(data, aes(x = StatsCourses, y = Judgment)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Statistics Credits and Fake-News Detection",
    x = "Statistics course credits (ECs)",
    y = "Correct judgements"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 3. Prepare the analysis dataset
```{r}
# do not automatically remove participants based on
# comprehension or guessed study purpose
# First inspect missingness and justify any exclusions.

analysis_data <- data %>%
  select(ID, StatsCourses, Judgment, Comprehension) %>%
  drop_na()

nrow(analysis_data)
```

### 4. RQ1
```{r}
# Association between statistics credits
# and the number of correct judgements

model_rq1 <- lm(
  Judgment ~ StatsCourses,
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(model_rq1)
confint(model_rq1)

# Check basic linear-model diagnostics
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_rq1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### 5. RQ2
```{r}
# Does comprehension moderate the association?
# Center the continuous predictors to aid interpretation

analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    StatsCourses_c = StatsCourses - mean(StatsCourses),
    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension)
  )

model_rq2 <- lm(
  Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c,
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(model_rq2)
confint(model_rq2)

# Inspect the interaction visually
ggplot(
  analysis_data,
  aes(
    x = StatsCourses,
    y = Judgment,
    color = factor(
      if_else(Comprehension >= median(Comprehension),
              "Higher comprehension", "Lower comprehension")
    )
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Statistics course credits (ECs)",
    y = "Correct judgements",
    color = "Comprehension group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# 8. Extract model estimates for reporting

tidy(model_rq1, conf.int = TRUE)
tidy(model_rq2, conf.int = TRUE)

glance(model_rq1)
glance(model_rq2)
```

## Part B: Check Computational Reproducitibility
### 1. Inspect the dataset
```{r}

head(a2_data)
str(a2_data)
dim(a2_data)
names(a2_data)
summary(a2_data)

# Check duplicate participant IDs

# Check whether values fall within the ranges
# specified in the assignment
summary(a2_data$StatsCourses)
summary(a2_data$GradeStats)
summary(a2_data$Judgment)
summary(a2_data$Comprehension)
summary(a2_data$GradeStats)
summary(a2_data$ReadNews)

# Check categorical variable

```

### 2. Prepare the dataset, one with 5.5 as the passing-grade threshold,
### another one with 6.0
```{r}
# Remove participants who guessed the study goal
# and participants with a non-passing statistics grade

clean_data_1 <- a2_data %>%
  filter(GoalStudy == 0,
         GradeStats >= 5.5)

# Check remaining sample size
nrow(clean_data_1)

# Check the cleaned dataset
summary(clean_data_1)
```

```{r}
# Try 6.0 as the passing grade
clean_data_2 <- a2_data %>%
  filter(GoalStudy == 0,
         GradeStats >= 6.0)

# Check remaining sample size
nrow(clean_data_2)

# Check the cleaned dataset
summary(clean_data_2)
```

```{r}

```

## 5. rq2
```{r}
# Mean-centering
clean_data_1 <- clean_data_1 %>%
  mutate(
    StatsCourses_c = StatsCourses - mean(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
clean_data_2 <- clean_data_2 %>%
  mutate(
    StatsCourses_c = StatsCourses - mean(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
# Model 2.1: Moderation analysis with 5.5 as passing grade

model2_1 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c +
               ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_1)

# View results
summary(model2_1)
```

```{r}
# Model 2.2: Moderation analysis with 6.0 as passing grade

model2_2 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c +
               ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_2)

# View results
summary(model2_2)
```


### 6. Regression assumptions check
```{r}

```

```{r}

plot(model2_1, which=2)
```

```{r}
# Homoscedasticity

bptest(model2_2)
```

```{r}
# Multicollinearity

vif(model2_2)
```

## Part D: Conducting the Multiverse Analysis
```{r}
dat <- read.csv("A1_data.csv")   
str(dat)
```
Check that the exclusion counts in our decision list:

```{r}
c(goal    = sum(dat$GoalStudy == 1),
  grade55 = sum(dat$GradeStats < 5.5),
  grade60 = sum(dat$GradeStats < 6.0),
  comp7   = sum(dat$Comprehension <= 7),
  comp10  = sum(dat$Comprehension <= 10))
```

## The multiverse

Every row of `grid` is one pathway: 2 × 3 × 4 × 3 = 72 combinations.

```{r}
grid <- expand.grid(
  goal  = c("Keep", "Exclude"),
  grade = c("Keep all", "< 5.5", "< 6.0"),
  comp  = c("Keep all", "<= 7", "<= 10", "Covariate"),
  covs  = c("None", "ReadNews", "ReadNews + Sexe"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
nrow(grid)
```

`run_path()` takes the four choices, applies the exclusions (D1–D3),
builds the regression formula (D3 covariate option + D4) and returns the
estimate for StatsCourses. Comprehension only enters the model through D3,
so it can never be added twice.

```{r}
run_path <- function(goal, grade, comp, covs) {
  d <- dat
  if (goal == "Exclude") d <- d[d$GoalStudy == 0, ]
  if (grade == "< 5.5")  d <- d[d$GradeStats >= 5.5, ]
  if (grade == "< 6.0")  d <- d[d$GradeStats >= 6.0, ]
  if (comp == "<= 7")    d <- d[d$Comprehension > 7, ]
  if (comp == "<= 10")   d <- d[d$Comprehension > 10, ]

  predictors <- c("StatsCourses",
                  if (comp == "Covariate") "Comprehension",
                  if (covs != "None") "ReadNews",
                  if (covs == "ReadNews + Sexe") "Sexe")
  fit <- lm(reformulate(predictors, response = "Judgment"), data = d)

  ci <- confint(fit)["StatsCourses", ]
  data.frame(n        = nobs(fit),
             estimate = coef(fit)[["StatsCourses"]],
             lower    = ci[[1]],
             upper    = ci[[2]],
             p        = summary(fit)$coefficients["StatsCourses", "Pr(>|t|)"])
}

results <- cbind(grid, do.call(rbind, Map(run_path, grid$goal, grid$grade,
                                          grid$comp, grid$covs)))
rownames(results) <- NULL

write.csv(results, "multiverse_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Summary

The estimate is the change in correct judgements per extra credit (EC).
The research question is directional, so we count a pathway as support when
the estimate is positive and p < .05 (two-sided, which is conservative).

```{r}
results$support <- results$estimate > 0 & results$p < .05

c(pathways      = nrow(results),
  share_support = mean(results$support),
  median_est    = median(results$estimate),
  min_est       = min(results$estimate),
  max_est       = max(results$estimate),
  min_n         = min(results$n),
  max_n         = max(results$n))
```

Median estimate per option, to see which decision moves the result most.

```{r}
for (d in c("goal", "grade", "comp", "covs")) {
  print(tapply(results$estimate, results[[d]], median))
}
```

## Specification curve

Top: the 72 estimates sorted from small to large, with 95% CIs.
Bottom: which choice each pathway made for each decision.

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
results <- results[order(results$estimate), ]
results$rank <- seq_len(nrow(results))

top <- ggplot(results, aes(rank, estimate, colour = support)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), size = 0.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#4472C4", "FALSE" = "grey60"),
                      breaks = c("TRUE", "FALSE"),
                      labels = c("positive, p < .05", "not significant"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Estimate for StatsCourses") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_blank())

choices <- data.frame(
  rank     = rep(results$rank, 4),
  decision = rep(c("D1 Goal", "D2 Grade", "D3 Comprehension", "D4 Covariates"),
                 each = nrow(results)),
  choice   = c(results$goal, results$grade, results$comp, results$covs)
)

bottom <- ggplot(choices, aes(rank, choice)) +
  geom_point(shape = "|", size = 3) +
  facet_grid(decision ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Pathway (sorted by estimate)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))

top / bottom + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 3))
# save plot
spec_curve <- top / bottom + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 3))
spec_curve
ggsave("specification_curve.pdf", spec_curve, width = 10, height = 8)
```
